S16.01.note: Expected mentions an avatar, but the code draws no avatar; the author is told apart by alignment and bubble style, and the name appears only to screen readers.
steps: Sign in, open a chat (or start a new one), type "Hello" in the message box and send it.
Look at your message: it sits on the right in a rounded bubble.
Look at the reply: it is plain text across the full width with no bubble.
Turn on a screen reader and move to your message: it is announced as "Your message: Hello" (the name "You" is only in that spoken label).
Compare with Expected: alignment and bubble style tell the two authors apart; no avatar or visible name was found in the code.
S16.01.where: Chat > send any message > look at your message and the reply

steps: In a chat, type a short sentence in the message box.
Tap send.
Look at the transcript: the sentence you sent appears in your message bubble, unchanged.
S16.02.where: Chat > send any message > your message in the transcript

S16.03.needs: a file or image to upload
S16.03.note: The attach button's visible words were not found; if the file is missing from the phone, the app shows the alert "Could not open file" instead.
steps: In a chat, use the attach control in the message box to choose a photo or a file. The control's exact label was not checked in the code.
Send the message.
Look at the sent message: an image appears as a tile, and a file appears as a chip with its name and a detail line.
Tap the image tile (hint "Opens full screen") or the file chip (hint "Opens the file") and check it opens.
S16.03.where: Chat > attach a file or image in the message box > send > the sent message

S16.04.note: Searched MessageBubble.tsx: the only chips on a sent user message are a quoted-text chip (text starting with "> " then a blank line) and a "Skill: " chip. No code adds connector, page, editor-selection or @mention chips to a sent message.

steps: Press and hold your sent message (about 0.4 seconds) to open the message actions.
Tap "Copy Message".
Paste into the message box.
Compare the pasted text with the sent message: it must match. (While a reply is still streaming the label reads "Copy Partial Response".)
S16.07.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Copy Message

S16.08.needs: a sent message in a chat
S16.08.note: If an answer has unsaved edits, the app first asks before the edit replaces that answer.
steps: Press and hold your sent message and tap "Edit Message".
In the "Edit Message" dialog, change the text in the box labelled "Edit message text".
Tap "Send".
Look for a new reply to the edited text and the version pager ("1 / 2" style) under your message.
S16.08.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Edit Message

S16.09.needs: a sent message in a chat
S16.09.note: The action is hidden when the app reports that rerun is unavailable.
steps: Press and hold your sent message to open the message actions.
Tap "Resend" without changing the text.
Look at the transcript: a fresh reply appears for the same message.
S16.09.where: Chat > long-press your sent message > Resend

S16.11.needs: a sent message that has been edited
S16.11.note: The label is built from the word "version" in code, so the spoken label reads "Previous version"; the pager appears only when the message has more than one version.
steps: Edit a sent message and send the edit, so the message has two versions.
Under the edited message, look for the pager with a left and right arrow and a count such as "2 / 2".
Tap the left arrow (screen-reader label "Previous version").
Check the count changes to "1 / 2" and the thread shows the earlier version and its reply. Tap the right arrow to go back.
S16.11.where: Chat > Edit Message on a sent message (S16.08) > version pager under your message

S16.15.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
S16.15.note: The failed badge appears only when an offline-queued message fails to go out; other send errors show as a banner on the chat screen, not on the bubble.
steps: Turn off the network on the test device.
In a chat, type a message and send it: the bubble shows a "queued" badge.
Turn the network back on and wait for the send to finish.
If the send fails, look at the bubble: it shows "failed to send" with a "Retry" button.
S16.15.where: Chat > send a message with the network off > the failed message bubble

S16.16.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
S16.16.note: Attachments are restored from the stored message before the retry is sent (chatExecutionStore.ts), and the retry count is limited with the alert "Retry Limit Reached".
steps: Make a send fail as in S16.15 so the bubble shows "failed to send".
Tap "Retry" next to it (or long-press the message and tap "Resend").
Check the same text and attached files are sent again.
Check the failed badge goes away and a reply appears, or a new failure replaces it.

S16.17.needs: a chat where a reply is still running (or the network off for the offline badge)
S16.17.note: The row above the box shows only the message text with a clock icon and no visible "queued" word was checked; the "queued" badge belongs to offline sends.
steps: Send a message and, while its reply is still streaming, type a second message and tap send.
Look above the message box: the second message appears as a row with a clock icon, with an "Edit queued message" and a "Cancel queued message" button.
Wait for the first reply to finish: the queued message goes out and appears in the transcript.
Optionally, with the network off, send a message: its bubble shows the "queued" badge until it goes out.
S16.17.where: Chat > send a second message while a reply is still running > the row above the message box

S16.18.needs: a way to turn the network off on the test device
S16.18.note: Drafts are stored per chat (draftKey is the chat id in app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx); no visible word "draft" was found in the code.
steps: In a chat, type a sentence but do not send it. Open another chat, then come back: the sentence is still in the message box for this chat.
In the first chat, send the sentence with the network off (see S16.15) so the send fails.
Check the sentence returns to the message box as unsent text, and that it does not appear as a sent message in the transcript.
Compare: sent messages appear in the transcript, while the unsent text stays in the box.
S16.18.where: Chat > type in the message box without sending > switch chats and come back; and a failed send
